decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run:
br-9sxrn / br-kp1in.13 A/B decision rule. Written 2026-10-11 ~02:45Z, before any arm was built or run.

Arms (release builds, same host, same session):
  base     = main a413ddb5 (WAL reset gate + reservation staging already in)
  stage    = base + message bundles staged and synced outside the archive fence (renames, the id-collision check and digest appends stay under it)
  stagepar = stage + staging fsyncs on up to 8 threads for sets of >= 8 files

Runs:
  P. Paced, equal offered load: paced_swarm.py, 60 agents, period 6 s, 300 s, order base stage stagepar stagepar stage base.
  R. Release smoke via `am e2e run release_smoke`, candidate vs control in one invocation, both orders, for stage vs base and stagepar vs base.

Primary (br-9sxrn probe): the soak check "WBQ drained_total advances in every 10s window with queued work" PASSES for the arm in both orders, with soak sends >= 4000.

Guards (any failure means the arm LOSES and is not landed):
  G1. Release smoke swarm send p99 is no more than 20% above base's in either order.
  G2. Release smoke client errors (swarm + soak) are no more than base's + 5 in either order; the durability, integrity and convergence checks pass.
  G3. Paced: the last-60 s send p90 and the overall send p99 are no more than 20% above base's in either round.

Secondary (br-kp1in.13): release smoke swarm reservation p99 against the 5 s bound, and paced reservation p50/p90.

Landing:
  - Land the smaller arm (stage before stagepar) that meets the primary and all guards.
  - If neither meets the primary, an arm that meets every guard and cuts swarm reservation p99 by >= 25% vs base in both orders lands as br-kp1in.13 progress, and br-9sxrn stays open.
  - Otherwise report the loss on both beads and land nothing.

paced_equal_load_at_swarm_send_rate.decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run:
ab13b: equal-offered-load check at the swarm's send rate. Written 2026-10-11 ~06:05Z, after smoke R1
(stage_vs_base) and before R2-R4 or any ab13b run.

Why: in R1, guard G1 of ab13_rule.txt failed for 'stage'. Its closed-loop swarm send p99 was 5.27 s vs
4.30 s (+22.6%; the limit is +20%), while it completed 8,152 sends vs 5,647 (+44%). G1 stays failed as
written; this experiment does not change ab13_rule.txt. It answers one question: at EQUAL offered work
near that rate, are sends slower on the arm?
  - If they are not, the G1 failure comes from the arm doing more work against a capped send path
    (br-qbhs0), not from slower sends.
  - If they are, it is a real send regression (for example, staging fsyncs contending with
    database commits).

Runs: paced_swarm.py, 60 agents, period 2 s (~30 sends/s, 30 fetches/s, ~9 reserve+release/s offered),
300 s. Order: base stage stagepar stagepar stage base. Same binaries as ab13 (build14), same host,
one invocation, nothing else of mine running locally.

Reading, per arm vs base, in BOTH rounds:
  S1. Overall send p90 and p99 are no more than 1.2x base's.
  S2. Last-60 s send p90 is no more than 1.2x base's.
  If S1 and S2 hold in both rounds, then at equal work the arm's sends are not slower.
  Otherwise it is a measured send regression, and the arm does not land whatever the smoke says.

Reported alongside: reservation p50/p90/p99, errors, end-of-run WAL size, and per-60 s send p50/p90.

Landing remains governed by ab13_rule.txt with G1 recorded as FAILED. A decision to land despite G1
needs the user's or owner's call, presented with both results. ab13b alone does not authorize it.
paced_equal_load_at_swarm_send_rate.method: paced_swarm.py: 60 agents, period 2 s (~30 sends/s offered), 300 s; same build14 binaries; WAL size sampled every 5 s

verdict:
LOSS under the predeclared rules (ab13_rule.txt, ab13b_rule.txt). Not landed.

Measured:
- Fence: staging message bundles outside ARCHIVE_PUBLICATION_FENCE removes the fence as a bottleneck. Both
  arms logged 0 contended fence waits >= 2 s in every release-smoke run, vs 3,650-3,753 for base. The base
  holders were the WBQ bundle batch (lib.rs:3523) and single bundle ops (lib.rs:3613).
- Paced at equal offered load (period 6 s, ~10 sends/s):
  - reservation p90 is 0.22 s vs 3.25-3.53 s, and p99 is 0.46-0.65 s vs 7.0-8.3 s;
  - send p99 is 1.47-2.59 s vs 2.45-6.42 s, and last-60 s send p90 is within +15% of base (guard G3 met).
- Release smoke (closed loop), all four runs:
  - reservation p99 is 1.37-2.75 s vs 17.7-30.0 s, with 0 vs 4-43 thirty-second timeouts;
  - swarm sends are 23-54% higher.
  - stagepar passes the soak 'WBQ drained_total advances in every 10s window' check in both orders
    (5,176 and 5,228 soak sends). Base and stage fail it in both orders.
  - Guard G1 (swarm send p99 <= 1.2x base in both orders) FAILS: stage is +22.6% (R1), stagepar +25% (R3).
    The other order passes for both.
  - Errors are of the same order as base, and the crash/integrity checks pass in all arms. Post-swarm archive
    convergence fails in every arm, base included.
- Paced at equal work near the swarm rate (period 2 s; both arms saturate and overrun the schedule):
  - send p50 is 2.8-3.2 s vs 0.65-0.67 s, and p90 is 3.8-4.3 s vs 1.86-2.02 s. Rule S1 FAILS for both arms.
  - The same work finishes 15-17% sooner (565-580 s vs 665-680 s), and reservation p99 is 1.6-2.5 s vs 14.6-15.3 s.
  - Server database_write p99 is 9-17 ms in every arm, so there is no consistent per-write slowdown.
  - The WBQ queue p99 is 81-86 s for stage, 2-7 s for stagepar and 13-14 s for base. Base's commit-queue p99
    is 533-577 s.

Reading: below saturation sends are unaffected. At saturation the fence no longer throttles agents through
their reservations, so they queue on the message send path instead: the serialized id election and insert
(br-qbhs0 / br-sa58k). That path is now the binding constraint. Parallel staging is what keeps the archive
drain inside the 10 s window (staging alone does not).

Next: raise send-path capacity (br-qbhs0), then rerun this A/B. Patches are kept: 13_stage_bundles_S_lib.patch
and 13_stage_bundles_SP_lib.patch. Landing as-is is the owner's call (reservation timeouts and fence stalls
vs send latency at saturation).
